platforms.name: Unconjugated (naked) PMO — approved class plus dual-targeting next generation (brogidirsen)
platforms.architecture: Phosphorodiamidate morpholino oligomer, uncharged, no ligand. Uptake is non-receptor-mediated and favours leaky dystrophic fibres. Brogidirsen (NS-089/NCNP-02, Nippon Shinyaku) is a single PMO containing two connected sequences against two sites in the same exon — a payload-potency innovation, not a delivery one.
platforms.reaches_cell: Skeletal muscle myofibres: yes, but inefficiently; delivery is highest in actively degenerating/regenerating fibres. Heart: historically poor-to-absent — 'early in vivo mouse studies using systemic PMO have consistently shown poor or absent dystrophin restoration in the heart' (PMC6005479). Diaphragm reached less well than limb muscle. Satellite cells: not meaningfully. CNS: no (no BBB penetration after IV).
platforms.functional_activity: Yes — splice switching is intracellular and productive, confirmed by RT-PCR skipped transcript and western-blot dystrophin in four FDA-approved drugs. Magnitude is usually low, except where the exon target is unusually amenable.
platforms.human_pd: Eteplirsen (exon 51, 30 mg/kg/wk): ~0.4% of normal dystrophin at 48 wks, ~0.9% at 188 wks. Golodirsen (exon 53): 0.095%→1.019% at wk48. Casimersen (exon 45): 0.93%→1.74% at wk48. Viltolarsen (exon 53, 40 and 80 mg/kg/wk): 0.3%→5.7% and 0.6%→5.9% at wk25. Brogidirsen (exon 44, 40 and 80 mg/kg/wk, 24 wks): 10.27% and 15.79% of normal in one report, 16.63% and 24.47% in another; Phase 1/2 mean change +13.1% (p=0.03). No human cardiac dystrophin data for any of them.
platforms.dose_frequency: Weekly IV infusion, 30–80 mg/kg, indefinitely. Weekly infusion burden is a major real-world disadvantage versus Q4W/Q6W conjugates.
platforms.toxicity: Best-characterised safety record in the field; years of weekly dosing. Main issues are infusion reactions and renal-tubular monitoring (proteinuria, cystatin C); hypomagnesemia/eGFR decline seen with PPMOs is not a feature of naked PMO. Brogidirsen reported long-term safety with stable motor function.
platforms.access: Highest buildability. No delivery IP to license; PMO chemistry and CMC are commoditised with multiple CDMOs, and a 2-oligo cocktail for a 54+55 double skip is straightforward to manufacture and file as separate or combined drug substance. The dual-sequence connected design is Nippon Shinyaku IP and would need freedom-to-operate review if copied.

findings.claim: Viltolarsen accelerated approval rested on dystrophin rising 0.3%→5.7% (40 mg/kg) and 0.6%→5.9% (80 mg/kg) of normal at week 25.
Golodirsen 0.095%→1.019%, casimersen 0.93%→1.74% of normal at week 48; eteplirsen ~0.4% at 48 weeks.
Brogidirsen, an unconjugated dual-sequence PMO, reached 10.27–15.79% (one report 16.63–24.47%) of normal dystrophin at 40/80 mg/kg weekly for 24 weeks.
Systemic naked PMO has consistently shown poor or absent dystrophin restoration in heart.

platforms.name: Anti-TfR1 monoclonal antibody–PMO conjugate (Avidity AOC; del-zota / AOC 1044)
platforms.architecture: Full IgG monoclonal antibody against transferrin receptor 1 (TfR1/CD71), non-cleavable linker, PMO cargo. TfR1 is highly expressed on skeletal and cardiac myocytes.
platforms.reaches_cell: Skeletal muscle: yes, clinically demonstrated by biopsy exon-skipping and dystrophin. Heart: demonstrated in animals only — mouse-active variant gave dose-dependent cardiac dystrophin (reported up to ~5% of wild-type in hDMD/exon-45-del mice) and NHPs showed dose-dependent PMO concentration and exon-44 skipping across muscles including heart. No human cardiac biopsy. CNS: not claimed for the muscle-optimised conjugate; TfR1 is separately an established BBB shuttle receptor, so CNS reach is a plausible but unproven extension, not something to assume.
platforms.functional_activity: Yes, and the strongest functional evidence in the class: biopsy-confirmed skipped transcript, dystrophin protein, and >80% fall in serum creatine kinase toward normal — a downstream marker that the restored protein is protecting membranes.
platforms.human_pd: EXPLORE44, 5 mg/kg × 3 doses Q6W, n=10 at 4 months: statistically significant +37% exon-44 skipping (up to 66% skipping observed) and +25% of normal dystrophin, mean dystrophin ~32% and up to 54% of normal; CK reduced >80% from baseline to near-normal.
platforms.dose_frequency: 5 mg/kg IV every 6 weeks — the lowest dose and least frequent schedule of any clinically active DMD exon-skipping agent.
platforms.toxicity: Favourable in EXPLORE44/OLE; most TEAEs mild or moderate. Class watch-items for TfR1 agents remain reticulocyte/erythroid effects and infusion reactions; retrieved sources report no reduction in receptor protein with repeat dosing for TfR1 ligands generally. No hypomagnesemia signal reported.
platforms.access: Effectively closed. Avidity was acquired by Novartis (~$12bn, agreed Oct 2025, closing H1 2026) specifically for the AOC delivery platform; del-zota's BLA was accepted for priority review under accelerated approval on 8 Sep 2026 with Phase 3 SAFARI44 as confirmatory. A new exon-54/55 asset on this platform would require a Novartis partnership, which is realistic only as an in-licence of our sequence into their platform, not the reverse.

findings.claim: Del-zota 5 mg/kg Q6W (3 doses, n=10, 4 months): +25% of normal dystrophin, +37% exon-44 skipping (up to 66%), CK down >80%.
AOC 1044 restored dystrophin in skeletal and cardiac muscle in a DMD mouse model; NHPs showed dose-dependent exon-44 skipping across muscles including heart.
FDA accepted the del-zota BLA for priority review under accelerated approval on 8 September 2026; SAFARI44 Phase 3 is the confirmatory trial.
Novartis agreed to acquire Avidity for $12bn to gain its RNA-targeting muscle delivery platform.

platforms.name: Anti-TfR1 Fab–PMO conjugate (Dyne FORCE; DYNE-251 / z-rostudirsen)
platforms.architecture: Fab fragment against TfR1, cleavable linker, PMO cargo. Smaller than a full IgG, intended to improve tissue penetration and reduce Fc-mediated effects.
platforms.reaches_cell: Skeletal muscle: yes, biopsy-confirmed. Heart: preclinical only — FORCE-M23D gave robust skipping and durable dystrophin restoration in mdx mice, with the platform described as delivering to skeletal and cardiac muscle; no human cardiac dystrophin measurement retrieved. Respiratory: lung function reported preserved at 6 months (functional, not tissue, evidence). CNS: not claimed.
platforms.functional_activity: Yes — dystrophin protein plus functional signals (Stride Velocity 95th Centile improvement exceeding the proposed MCID, sustained to 18–24 months).
platforms.human_pd: DELIVER: 20 mg/kg Q4W at 6 months, n=8 — 3.71% of normal dystrophin unadjusted, 8.72% muscle-content-adjusted (>10-fold the 0.3% reported for eteplirsen). Registrational Expansion Cohort primary endpoint met: 5.46% of normal muscle-content-adjusted, 7-fold from baseline, p<0.0001.
platforms.dose_frequency: 20 mg/kg IV every 4 weeks (10, 20 and 40 mg/kg cohorts studied).
platforms.toxicity: 54 participants, ~675 doses, >50 patient-years: most TEAEs mild or moderate; 2 serious adverse events in the 40 mg/kg group, both recovered — i.e. a dose ceiling is visible above 20 mg/kg.
platforms.access: Dyne is independent and the platform is its core asset; a partnership or cargo-in-licence for a new exon target is conceivable but Dyne is mid-registration (US accelerated-approval submission targeted Q2 2026) and will prioritise its own pipeline. Treat as partner-dependent, not internally buildable.

findings.claim: DYNE-251 20 mg/kg Q4W: 8.72% of normal dystrophin (muscle-content adjusted) at 6 months, n=8; 54-participant safety set with 2 SAEs at 40 mg/kg.

Registrational Expansion Cohort met primary endpoint: 5.46% of normal muscle-content-adjusted dystrophin at 6 months, 7-fold from baseline, p<0.0001; US accelerated approval submission planned Q2 2026.
FORCE Fab-TfR1 conjugation of an exon-skipping PMO gave dose-dependent skipping and durable dystrophin restoration in mdx mice.

platforms.name: Cell-penetrating peptide–PMO (PPMO): Sarepta SRP-5051/vesleteplirsen, PepGen EDO, preclinical Pip6a-PMO
platforms.architecture: Cationic arginine-rich or related cell-penetrating peptide covalently fused to PMO; receptor-independent, charge-driven uptake and endosomal escape.
platforms.reaches_cell: Best preclinical cardiac reach of any PMO format: Pip6a-PMO gave 37.2% dystrophin in mdx and 51.6% in Cmah-/-mdx hearts with normalised cardiac output and restored ventricular function — proof that cardiomyocytes are reachable. In humans, however, the clinical PPMOs were limited by toxicity or insufficient exposure. CNS: no.
platforms.functional_activity: Yes in animals (cardiac contractile reserve corrected). In humans SRP-5051 gave 18× the exon skipping and 8× the dystrophin of eteplirsen; PepGen's EDO51 produced skipped transcript but almost no protein.
platforms.human_pd: SRP-5051 30 mg/kg monthly, 12 weeks: 18× exon skipping and 8× dystrophin versus eteplirsen 30 mg/kg weekly × 24 weeks. PGN-EDO51 10 mg/kg: exon-51 skipped transcripts 4.26% but total dystrophin only 0.59% of normal.
platforms.dose_frequency: Monthly IV (SRP-5051 30 mg/kg Q4W; PGN-EDO51 up to 10 mg/kg Q4W).
platforms.toxicity: The reason this class failed. SRP-5051: hypomagnesemia, in some participants prolonged after stopping, plus eGFR decline; dosing stopped 6 Nov 2024 and the programme was discontinued on long-term safety/tolerability grounds. PGN-EDO51 was itself well tolerated (all related AEs mild, no SAEs) but was discontinued in May 2025 because PepGen could not dose high enough for meaningful dystrophin. Pip6a-PMO killed 5/15 mice at 18 mg/kg fortnightly, suggesting cumulative toxicity.
platforms.access: PepGen's EDO platform is explicitly open to partnering/licensing and the company has exited DMD, so the chemistry is obtainable cheaply — but it is obtainable because it did not work at tolerated doses in DMD. Sarepta's PPMO is deprioritised. Do not build the lead on this class; it is useful only as chemistry/dosing precedent and a cardiac-reach existence proof.

findings.claim: SRP-5051 30 mg/kg monthly gave 18× exon skipping and 8× dystrophin versus weekly eteplirsen, but prolonged hypomagnesemia and eGFR decline led to discontinuation; dosing stopped 6 Nov 2024.
PGN-EDO51 at 10 mg/kg reached 4.26% exon-51 skipped transcript but only 0.59% of normal dystrophin; PepGen discontinued all DMD work in May 2025.
Pip6a-PMO achieved 37.2% (mdx) and 51.6% (Cmah-/-mdx) cardiac dystrophin with normalised cardiac output, but 5/15 mice died at 18 mg/kg fortnightly.

platforms.name: Endosomal Escape Vehicle cyclic peptide–PMO (Entrada ENTR-601-44)
platforms.architecture: Proprietary cyclic cell-penetrating peptide (EEV) conjugated to PMO, designed for endosomal escape rather than receptor targeting.
platforms.reaches_cell: Skeletal muscle: yes, with dose-dependent muscle drug exposure and skipping shown at WMS 2026. Heart and CNS: no human data retrieved.
platforms.functional_activity: Partial. Biomarker shifts are modest but Time-to-Rise velocity improved versus placebo with statistical significance, reported as ~3.5× the MCID — functional benefit out of proportion to the protein increase, which is a flag to interpret cautiously rather than a validated effect.
platforms.human_pd: ELEVATE-44-201 Cohort 1 (reported May 2026): +2.36% dystrophin over a 4.00% baseline and +2.31% exon skipping over a 2.66% baseline. Dose escalation continues; Cohort 3 goes up to 18 mg/kg with data expected after year-end 2026.
platforms.dose_frequency: IV, escalating cohorts up to 18 mg/kg; exact interval not specified in the sources retrieved.
platforms.toxicity: Met primary safety objectives in Cohort 1; a prior FDA clinical hold on the programme was removed. No hypomagnesemia-type signal retrieved.
platforms.access: Entrada is independent, mid-dose-escalation, and running parallel exon 44/45/50/51 programmes — partnering for a new exon target is possible but the platform's delivered dystrophin so far (~2–3 percentage points) is well below the TfR1 conjugates. Second-tier option.

findings.claim: ENTR-601-44 Cohort 1: +2.36% dystrophin over 4.00% baseline, +2.31% exon skipping over 2.66% baseline; Time-to-Rise improved vs placebo exceeding MCID ~3.5-fold.
At WMS 2026 Entrada showed dose-dependent exposure, muscle delivery and increased exon skipping at higher doses; Cohort 3 goes to 18 mg/kg.

platforms.name: TfR1-binding bicyclic peptide–oligonucleotide conjugate (Ionis/Bicycle, BCY17901) — preclinical
platforms.architecture: ~2 kDa synthetic bicyclic peptide ligand for TfR1 conjugated to ASO or siRNA. Keeps receptor targeting but is a fully synthetic small conjugate rather than a biologic, so CMC resembles oligo manufacture, not antibody manufacture.
platforms.reaches_cell: Skeletal muscle and heart in human-TfR1 knock-in mice and cynomolgus monkeys. Demonstrated with Dmpk/Malat1 ASOs and Hprt siRNA, not yet with a DMD exon-skipping cargo — and PMO cargo compatibility is not established in what was retrieved.
platforms.functional_activity: Yes for RNase-H and RNAi cargoes: 5.2–8.4× potency gain in quadriceps, 6.9–7.6× in gastrocnemius and ≥5.8× in heart versus unconjugated. Single-nucleus sequencing showed activity across fast- and slow-twitch fibre types.
platforms.human_pd: None found. No clinical data retrieved for this ligand class in muscle.
platforms.dose_frequency: Preclinical: 3.5 mg/kg IV or SC in mice; 25 mg/kg IV in NHP. A subcutaneous route is credible for this format, which no TfR1 antibody conjugate offers.
platforms.toxicity: No receptor protein depletion after repeated dosing; no off-target binding beyond TfR1 in high-throughput screening. No chronic-tox or human safety data.
platforms.access: Licensable in principle — Bicycle partners its ligands routinely and Ionis co-authored the work — but it is pre-IND for muscle and would need a PMO- or 2'-MOE-compatible linker built and validated for a splice-switching cargo. Realistic as a second-generation delivery bet behind a near-term lead, not as the first filing.

findings.claim: TfR1 bicyclic peptide BCY17901 conjugation improved ASO/siRNA potency 5.2–8.4× in quadriceps and ≥5.8× in heart in hTfR1 knock-in mice; 25 mg/kg IV tested in cynomolgus monkeys.

platforms.name: Other receptor-targeted and nanoparticle approaches (satellite-cell aptamer-gold, integrin α7β1) — preclinical only
platforms.architecture: Aptamer against α7/β1 integrin dimers on functionalised gold nanoparticles carrying nucleic-acid cargo; α7/β1 integrins are highly specific to muscle progenitors and myofibres and near-absent elsewhere.
platforms.reaches_cell: The only retrieved platform that explicitly targets muscle stem/satellite cells — the compartment that governs durability of correction in regenerating fibres, which is the one tissue the TfR1 conjugates do not address. Heart and CNS not addressed.
platforms.functional_activity: Reported delivery of microRNA into muscle stem cells promoting regeneration and improved muscle function in dystrophic mice; not shown with a splice-switching oligo.
platforms.dose_frequency: Local or systemic in mice; no translatable regimen.
platforms.toxicity: Not characterised for chronic systemic gold-nanoparticle dosing in humans; this is a material-accumulation risk for a lifelong therapy.
platforms.access: Academic (Nature Communications 2024); would be an internal build or academic collaboration. Research-stage only — relevant to the satellite-cell durability question in the brief, not to a near-term filing.

findings.claim: Aptamer-conjugated gold nanoparticles against α7/β1 integrin delivered oligonucleotide into muscle stem cells and improved dystrophic muscle function in mice.

naked_baseline: Best current unconjugated baseline for DMD exon skipping is brogidirsen (NS-089/NCNP-02), an unconjugated dual-sequence PMO against exon 44: 40 or 80 mg/kg IV weekly for 24 weeks gave 10.27% and 15.79% of normal dystrophin in one report and 16.63% and 24.47% in another, with a Phase 1/2 mean change from baseline of +13.1% (p=0.03) and reported long-term safety with stable motor function (https://www.cell.com/cell-reports-medicine/fulltext/S2666-3791(24)00672-4; https://www.neurologylive.com/view/brogidirsen-demonstrates-long-term-safety-stable-motor-function-dmd). The approved-drug baseline is far lower and defines what a generic naked PMO achieves: eteplirsen 30 mg/kg/wk ~0.4% of normal at 48 weeks and ~0.9% at 188 weeks; golodirsen 0.095%→1.019% at week 48; casimersen 0.93%→1.74% at week 48; viltolarsen 80 mg/kg/wk 0.6%→5.9% at week 25. All require weekly lifelong IV infusion. None has human cardiac dystrophin data, and systemic naked PMO shows poor or absent cardiac restoration in animals — so for a programme whose stated tissue list includes cardiomyocytes and diaphragm, naked PMO leaves the heart essentially untreated.
payload_vs_delivery: Delivery dominates the step from ~1% (eteplirsen/golodirsen/casimersen) to 5–9% (DYNE-251, same exon 51/53 biology, TfR1-conjugated). Target amenability and sequence potency dominate the exon-44 numbers: unconjugated brogidirsen reached 10–24% on exon 44, so del-zota's 25% is not a delivery benchmark transferable to a two-oligo exon 54+55 skip. Cardiac reach is purely delivery.
